title: Star acts and Lollipop Jones
summary: Singers, dancers and comedian Lollipop Jones, who Howard accompanied at the Lincoln Theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Who were some of the stars that came?

Well the stars, Alma Poinel, she was a star, singer-dAncer. Well the stars, Alma Poinnell, she was a star, singer, dancer. Harold was a Deja Jones wife, she was the leader of the chorus girls. And Melford Lewis, a lollipop comedian. Lollipop Jones? Lollipop Jones, yeah. Well I played a show for a lollipop in the early twenties, around twenty-seven or something like that, when he first came here with the Twenty Dots at the Lincoln Theater. See we was the regular band there, for the shows there, shows coming from out of town. And that's how I first met Lollipop then, but he was traveling. And I was to go with him, to travel on the road, and I didn't know. At that time I didn't care but going about. And something like a sweetie walker, and a comedian. What did Lollipop do?
What kind of act would he have?
Comedian, dance, tell jokes and so forth.
Comical. Comical? Dress up like what you call him, or be dressed up time, or what do you call his guy? Ray Skeleton? Same type. Yeah, beautiful clothes or something like that. Different thing.
He didn't put on a woman's costume, you know?
Oh. Yeah. Do you remember any of his jokes, any particular jokes about Lollipop that you could tell?
Yeah. It's been such a long time. Yeah. I just want to. Yeah. That overhand. Well it doesn't matter. I just wondered what kind of jokes he told.
I never saw him about those pictures and all that. Oh, he was good. They were really good. I really enjoyed it.
I'd be doing the show for them all the time, but I enjoyed it.
